extracted_concepts.name: Number
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Topic 1 covers integers, decimals, fractions, percentages, ratio, and rate.

extracted_concepts.name: Integer
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Whole numbers, including negative numbers, used in number operations.

extracted_concepts.name: Decimal
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Base-10 numbers used to represent parts of a whole.

extracted_concepts.name: Fraction
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A part of a whole written as numerator over denominator.

extracted_concepts.name: Percentage
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A ratio expressed as parts per hundred.

extracted_concepts.name: Ratio
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A comparison of quantities by division.

extracted_concepts.name: Rate
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A ratio comparing quantities with different units.

extracted_concepts.name: Standard form
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Scientific notation for very large or very small numbers.

extracted_concepts.name: Significant figures
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Digits that show the precision of a number.

extracted_concepts.name: Bounds of accuracy
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Upper and lower limits of a rounded measurement.

extracted_concepts.name: Algebraic expression
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A mathematical phrase with variables, constants, and operations.

extracted_concepts.name: Linear equation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: An equation with one variable raised to the first power.

extracted_concepts.name: Simultaneous linear equations
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Two or more linear equations solved together.

extracted_concepts.name: Quadratic equation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: An equation with a variable raised to the second power.

extracted_concepts.name: Inequality
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A statement using less than, greater than, or similar comparisons.

extracted_concepts.name: Sequence
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: An ordered list of numbers following a pattern.

extracted_concepts.name: Function
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A mapping that assigns each input exactly one output.

extracted_concepts.name: Cartesian coordinate system
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A plane formed by perpendicular axes using ordered pairs.

extracted_concepts.name: Gradient
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The slope or steepness of a line.

extracted_concepts.name: Equation of a straight line
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The linear relation y = mx + c on a coordinate plane.

extracted_concepts.name: Parallel lines
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Lines with the same gradient that never meet.

extracted_concepts.name: Perpendicular lines
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Lines whose gradients multiply to -1.

extracted_concepts.name: Mensuration
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Measurement of length, area, and volume.

extracted_concepts.name: Surface area
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The total area of the outside of a solid.

extracted_concepts.name: Arc length
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The length of part of a circle.

extracted_concepts.name: Sector area
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The area enclosed by two radii and an arc.

extracted_concepts.name: Angle properties
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Rules for angles in triangles, quadrilaterals, polygons, and circles.

extracted_concepts.name: Circle theorems
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Theorems about angles, arcs, and chords in circles.

extracted_concepts.name: Similarity
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Figures with the same shape but possibly different size.

extracted_concepts.name: Congruence
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Figures with the same shape and size.

extracted_concepts.name: Enlargement
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A transformation that changes size while preserving shape.

extracted_concepts.name: SOH CAH TOA
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Right-triangle trigonometric ratios for sine, cosine, and tangent.

extracted_concepts.name: Sine rule
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A rule relating sides and angles in non-right triangles.

extracted_concepts.name: Cosine rule
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A rule relating sides and angles in non-right triangles.

extracted_concepts.name: Vector
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A quantity with direction and magnitude, often written as a column vector.

extracted_concepts.name: Probability
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: The measure of the likelihood of an event.

extracted_concepts.name: Matrix
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A rectangular array of numbers used for operations and transformations.

extracted_relations.evidence: Topic 1 lists integers under Number.
Topic 1 lists decimals under Number.
Topic 1 lists fractions under Number.
Percentages express ratios out of 100.
A rate compares quantities using a ratio.
Standard form writes decimal numbers in scientific notation.
Bounds of accuracy depend on rounding and significant figures.
Linear equations are formed from algebraic expressions.
Simultaneous linear equations consist of linear equations.
Quadratic equations are algebraic equations.
Inequalities use algebraic expressions.
A sequence can be viewed as a function with integer inputs.
Straight-line equations are plotted on the Cartesian plane.
In y = mx + c, m is the gradient.
Parallel lines have equal gradients.
Perpendicular lines have gradients with product -1.
Surface area is a measurement topic.
Arc length is a measurement topic.
Sector area is a measurement topic.
Sector area is related to arc length.
Enlargement produces similar figures.
Congruence is a special case of similarity.
The sine rule extends right-triangle trigonometry.
The cosine rule extends right-triangle trigonometry.
Circle theorems use angle properties.
SOH CAH TOA uses angles in right triangles.
Vectors can be represented using coordinates.
Probability can be written as a ratio.
Matrices can represent simultaneous linear equations.
